title: Grateful Dead Live at Trouper's Hall on 1966-03-25

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear early‑66 soundboard capture with Pigpen’s thunderous organ and standout performances of “Hog For You,” “Hey Little One,” and “You Don’t Have to Ask.”
ai_review.review: This recording delivers an exceptionally clear early‑1966 Dead sound, letting Pigpen’s booming organ dominate while still showcasing Jerry’s fiery guitar work and the band’s tight R&B‑laden set. Reviewers rave about the superb renditions of “Hog For You,” “Hey Little One” and “You Don’t Have to Ask,” noting only occasional mix quirks like a loud organ level or a kick‑drum distortion that disappears in mono.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.5/5; the show is consistently praised for performance and energy, while recording quality is described as crystal clear with only minor mix issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear overall sound; vocals sometimes low, Pigpen’s organ a touch loud, occasional kick‑drum distortion on “Next Time You See Me,” and some reviewers note the mix sounds smoother in mono.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑66 set with a classic R&B feel; pre‑Primal Dead material that feels authentic and slightly slower than later years, but the flow is tight and the energy stays high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar sometimes a tad out of tune but overall fiery, shredding, and his impassioned vocals are praised as unforgettable.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass sits a little low in the mix yet remains solid; no major complaints about his playing.
band_member_comments.Bob: Briefly noted for “surf‑guitar extravaganza” alongside Jerry, contributing to the early‑66 vibe.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is described as thunderous, glorious, and the centerpiece of the performance—occasionally too loud but overwhelmingly positive.
band_member_comments.Drums: Kick drum distortion on one track noted; otherwise the rhythm section is solid.
